groups.name: Approval
groups.positive: Independence and maintaining a healthy sense of self-worth even when faced with criticism and disapproval.
groups.negative: The closer the score is to -10, the greater the excessive dependence on others' opinions — because self-assessment happens through 'borrowed' eyes. If someone criticizes this person, they automatically see themselves as worthless. Being emotionally oversensitive to what they believe others think of them makes them easy to manipulate. They are also vulnerable to anxiety and depression when others criticize or are angry with them.

groups.name: Love
groups.positive: The person treats love as something desirable but, beyond that, has many other equally important interests. Love is not a prerequisite for their happiness or self-esteem.
groups.negative: The person has a strong need for love and sees it as a prerequisite for survival and happiness. The closer the score is to -10, the stronger the dependency on love. Such a person tends to accept more subordinate, secondary roles in relationships with significant others, out of fear of being abandoned.

groups.name: Achievement
groups.positive: Deriving satisfaction from work and productivity, with the understanding that this is not the only or necessary way to maintain self-esteem.
groups.negative: This score is an indicator of work dependency. Such a person has a limited sense of self-worth and views themselves more like a commodity in a market. The closer the score is to -10, the more their joy and capacity for happiness depend on success and productivity.

groups.name: Perfectionism
groups.positive: The ability to set reasonable, flexible, and proportionate goals. The person enjoys the process of working toward a goal, rather than focusing solely on the outcome. They understand that they don't have to excel at everything or constantly strive to be outstanding.
groups.negative: Demanding perfection of oneself — mistakes are unacceptable, failure is worse than death, even negative emotions are a catastrophe. The closer the score is to -10, the more the person believes they must feel, think, and behave in an exceptionally perfect way, and if they don't, it feels as if everything is lost.

groups.name: Entitlement
groups.positive: The person does not feel 'destined' for certain things, so they make an effort to achieve what they want — and often succeed. They understand that everyone is unique, and there is no reason why fate should bend to their wishes.
groups.negative: Taking things like success, love, and happiness for granted. The closer the score is to -10, the more the person demands that those around them — and the entire universe — cater to their wishes in return for being good or working hard.

groups.name: Omnipotence
groups.positive: The person is content knowing that the world doesn't revolve around them. Since they don't control other adults, they are not responsible for them — only for themselves.
groups.negative: The presence of the cognitive distortion known as personalization. The closer the score is to -10, the more the person unjustifiably blames themselves for the faults and reactions of others that are beyond their control.

groups.name: Autonomy
groups.positive: The person's moods are generated by their own thoughts and attitudes, so they understand and accept responsibility for their own feelings.
groups.negative: The closer the score is to -10, the stronger the conviction that joy and satisfaction come from outside. This creates risk, because everything outside of us is outside our control. Such a person's mood becomes dependent on external factors.
